summary: Algiers wraps a wide Mediterranean bay. On its western peninsula sits Sidi Fredj, a 450-berth marina considered one of the finest on the sea's south shore; between it and the city is the El Djamila marina at Ain Benian; the central Port d'Alger fronts downtown; and across the water on the eastern shore, below the Roman ruins near Cap Matifou, lies the Tamentfoust harbour. All four ring the same bay minutes apart by boat but are chained today only by a congested coast road -- the classic case for a fast water shuttle.
